title: SAM Users’ Guide
text:
This website provides a user everything they need to know about the Standard Acquisition Methods (SAM) for commonly used datasets in planning applications python module.
sam utilizes the rpy2 library to interface with R for downloading census data and preforming some spatial operations. Currently, there isn’t a direct way to reference these libraries from the project environment that is setup by default and the below steps are needed to ensure rputils can load the R libraries

Install R (download from here: https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)
Open R terminal and run the following commands:

install.packages("tigris")
install.packages("sf")
install.packages("lwgeom")
install.packages("tidycensus")
sam will now use your system R install as the default when trying to utilize the downloader tools
For general useage see menus page for the specific submodules see submodules and for the raw download functions see downloaders
The source code for sam can be viewed here https://github.com/renaissanceplanning/sam.

title: Menus
text: For most non-technical users the menus submodule is sam’s one stop shop for data fetching. It provides a simple one line command to fetch all relevant data for a given project and set up a data directory. Currently only TOD projects are supported but future work will lead to additional menus which will be added to sam

title: Menus
text:
TOD Menu
The current TOD menu will download:

Census Geography
American Community Survey (ACS) Data including:

Age
Housing Costs and Values
Disability Status
Educational Attainment
Race and Ethnicity
Household Income, Size, Vehicles, and Workers
Ratio of Income to Poverty Level
Rent Costs
Housing Tenure

LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES):

Origin-Destination (OD)
Residence Area Characteristics (RAC)
Workplace Area Characteristics (WAC)

Florida Department of Revenue Parcels

Eventually a national set will need to be found.

Open Street Map Networks and Nodes

Bike
Pedestrian
Drive

HUD Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) Units


Code
The TOD Menu (and all future menus) will use a unified API that makes calls easy. All menus need to be supplied a summary area geodataframe. This summary area can come from any relevant shapefile so long as it covers the full project extent, for example a set of station area polygons, corridor polygons, or even urban growth boundary will work so long as they include the whole project area.
To use the menus the following code needs to be run in python:
import geopandas as gpd
from rputils import make_path
from sam.menus import pull_TOD_data

sum_area_path = make_path("path to shapefile")
data_dir = make_path("path to sharepoint data dir")

sum_area = gpd.read_file(sum_area_path)
prj_crs = sum_area.crs

pull_tod_data(
    summary_areas=sum_area,
    data_dir=data_dir,
    prj_crs=prj_crs,
)
It is worth noting that the coordinate system from the project (prj_crs) does not need to be the same as the summary area data frame and can be supplied in any format reconginzed by shapely however it is best practice to use teh summary area’s crs.
There are 3 additional arguments in the pull_tod_data function that can be modified:

lodes_data: Which LODES tables to fetch. Defaults to all avaliable LODES data sets.
lodes_level: Which geography to summarize LODES to. Defaults to Block Groups.
years (dict, optional): Years for parcel, acs, and lodes data. Defaults to most recent year avaliable.

title: Submodules
text: These submodules provide wrappers around the raw downloader functions and provide a uniform API across all data sets. These functions are generally unneeded as the menus already download this data, however some projects may need different requirements than the defaults and these submodules provide a convient way to change these defaults.

title: Submodules
text:
Config
Holds the default configuration files for sam, provides good examples of how they are formatted but should not be editted directly.

title: Submodules
text:
Reference Data
Provides useful datasets for cleaning. Do not edit.

title: Downloaders
text:
The raw downlaod functions, provide the most flexability to download the data but do not contain a uniform API and each function is different
Eventually will add the documentation.
